author: J. E. Johnston
content: Reports inadequate ammunition, easy turning above/below the river; proposes mobile troops to retard an enemy crossing and asks instructions; procuring wagons.
authority_or_effect: Request for mission clarification and conditional field employment.
receipt_evidence: Lee June1 acknowledges May26/28 communications (p897).
limitation: Enemy strength and vulnerability are Johnston assessments, not omniscient truth; receipt day not established.

author: J. E. Johnston
content: Regards the position as untenable against a strong enemy; proposes making the force movable to delay crossings and resist inland advance unless otherwise instructed.
authority_or_effect: Own proposed use of force under an unresolved mission.
receipt_evidence: No separate delivery stamp read.
limitation: Date is editorially bracketed; not an additional received government order.

author: J. E. Johnston
content: Describes widely spread detachments, river crossings and danger of enemy seizure of Martinsburg; asks precise instructions early; has prepared march transport; encloses Whiting memorandum.
authority_or_effect: Renews request to distinguish mobile force from garrison.
receipt_evidence: Lee June1 acknowledges May26/28 (p897).
limitation: Addressee editorially bracketed; original Whiting enclosure not established by this reading.

author: R. E. Lee
content: Describes Ewell/Hunton scouts; suggests joint attack with Bonham if a movement threatens the rear and Johnston cannot hold his position and judges it advisable.
authority_or_effect: Conditional operational suggestion; local judgment retained.
receipt_evidence: No delivery date read; June1 refers to earlier military arrangements (p897).
limitation: Not a simple order to move to Winchester; named threat and conditions matter.

author: J. E. Johnston
content: Relays reports of enemy concentration; asks whether troops should join another army rather than be lost here; warns that field equipment and wagons are insufficient.
authority_or_effect: Explicit proposal to leave the fixed point / be employed elsewhere.
receipt_evidence: Lee second June1 letter answers the May31 letter received by H. A. Edmundson (p897).
limitation: Intelligence is attributed hearsay; final route word is printed with an editorial question mark, so no route inferred from it.

author: R. E. Lee
content: Acknowledges May26/28; prefers reinforcement and retention; if unable to resist attack at all points, move out, destroy enemy-useful facilities, concentrate and contest inland advance; discretion in meeting a rear threat.
authority_or_effect: Conditional withdrawal instructions, not unconditional evacuation or hold at any cost.
receipt_evidence: Later letters discuss continuing instructions; exact receipt day not read.
limitation: Do not replace these conditions with a calendar departure.

author: R. E. Lee
content: Answers May31; sends available Staunton companies and Turney regiment; hopes position can be held; if opposed by too large a force repeats destruction/removal, rail denial, taking the field and checking advance up the valley.
authority_or_effect: Reinforced hold preference with an explicit conditional field alternative.
receipt_evidence: No exact receipt day read.
limitation: Removal/destruction is an instruction, not proof that every item was removed/destroyed.

author: R. E. Lee
content: Answers June1 intelligence; warns of political effect of abandonment and suggests a detachment towards Martinsburg or Opequon; announces reinforcement.
authority_or_effect: Continued preference for retention; does not erase prior conditional permissions.
receipt_evidence: Johnston June6 explicitly acknowledges this letter by last mail (pp907-908).
limitation: June1 covering letter p898 is the antecedent, not a departure authorization.

author: J. E. Johnston
content: Asks whether troops are a garrison or corps of observation; argues capture/destruction risk and difficult retreat; proposes delaying as prudently possible then transferring to a useful point; asks to understand his mission.
authority_or_effect: Answer/counterproposal to continued retention, not a refusal merely inferred from later movement.
receipt_evidence: Lee June7 says he received this letter and laid it before President (p910).
limitation: No new destination formally chosen in this paper; both proposed mission and receipt chain must be retained.

author: R. E. Lee relaying President views
content: Says President values Harpers Ferry and valley; doubts immediate Ohio attack; supplies and reinforcements promised; authorizes retirement if troops cannot successfully be opposed, leaving safety to Johnston judgment.
authority_or_effect: Conditional discretion within campaign purpose, alongside preference for retention.
receipt_evidence: No exact receipt day read.
limitation: Presidential view comes through Lee, not a separately read Davis-to-Johnston letter.

author: J. E. Johnston
content: Urges equipment before more troops are sent: new regiments divide inadequate ammunition and transport and make marching harder.
authority_or_effect: Material constraint on the proposed mobile mission.
receipt_evidence: No exact delivery date established in this packet.
limitation: Not by itself a fresh evacuation proposal or permission; do not convert into a temperament claim.

author: Jefferson Davis
content: Discusses retirement towards Winchester and Manassas railroad passes if attacked; expects valley support; rejects assumption that abandoning the valley for immediate junction is best; stresses transport limits.
authority_or_effect: Presidential campaign rationale and conditional alternatives.
receipt_evidence: Answers Beauregard June12 carried by Colonel Jones; that original is marked not found in OR.
limitation: Not addressed to Johnston; may not act as his received permission. No independent direct Davis reply to Johnston established here.

author: S. Cooper
content: Answers Whiting opinions endorsed by Johnston; explicitly authorizes withdrawal when enemy position convinces Johnston he is about to be turned; specifies destruction/removal, Winchester railway direction, conditional counterattack, and further retirement to Manassas-road passes if needed; promises support for free discretion.
authority_or_effect: Explicit conditional government authorization; preserves valley-defense purpose.
receipt_evidence: Johnston June15 acknowledges Cooper June13 (pp929-930); October report places a courier authorization June16 (p472).
limitation: Original endorsed Whiting paper not read; exact receipt sequence disputed; no blanket instruction to abandon valley or join Beauregard immediately.

author: S. Cooper
content: Says President sent to Johnston to dispatch an officer to Winchester, Jackson suggested, to rally people; hopes retirement if forced by a rear threat can lead to offensive action.
authority_or_effect: Corroborating government purpose and local assistance.
receipt_evidence: No Johnston receipt proved by a letter to Mason.
limitation: Do not turn this into a direct received Johnston order or proof of a mass turnout.

author: J. E. Johnston
content: Acknowledges June13 letter; disputes implication he wants others to bear responsibility; says he reported troop removal and other authorized matters to President the previous day.
authority_or_effect: Contemporaneous acknowledgment and report of action.
receipt_evidence: Acknowledged by June15; says letter just received at continuation on p930.
limitation: Previous-day report date is June14 [I]; original report to Davis not read. Does not reconcile October report June15 departure / June16 authorization.

author: J. E. Johnston
content: Says intelligence on morning June16 changed the perceived threat: no advance on Romney and expected crossing near Hagerstown; redirected troops to Bunker Hill to delay advance; describes himself twelve miles before Winchester.
authority_or_effect: Own operational choice based on received intelligence; seeks to conform to instructions received on 15th.
receipt_evidence: Cooper June18 says Thomas delivered June17 letter that day (p934).
limitation: Intelligence and force estimates are Johnston beliefs. Paper says instructions received on 15th; not silently equated to an unread June15 paper.

author: S. Cooper
content: Acknowledges June17; says any specificity in letter of 15th answered request, and expects Johnston to act as circumstances require to resist/repel invasion; asks frequent full reports; seeks remaining arms material from Harpers Ferry if possible.
authority_or_effect: Reaffirms continuing discretion and campaign limits.
receipt_evidence: June17 incoming letter delivered June18; no receipt date for this outgoing answer read.
limitation: Referenced Cooper June15 letter not located/read; do not substitute June13 automatically. Recovery request is not completed recovery.

author: S. Cooper
content: Acknowledges June18 letter; sends ammunition and urges prompt reports; stresses protecting valley communications and denying enemy-useful facilities.
authority_or_effect: Continuation of valley mission; address evidence.
receipt_evidence: Incoming June18 letter acknowledged June19; original not read here.
limitation: Near Winchester in address is not an exact army arrival date or building-level headquarters.

author: Johnston report dated 1861-10-14
content: Says Hill sent by rail June13 with Thirteenth and Tenth Virginia towards Romney via Winchester; heavy baggage and remaining public property sent by rail June13-14 and Potomac bridges destroyed.
authority_or_effect: Reported preparation and destruction before main departure.
receipt_evidence: Retrospective official report.
limitation: Not an original daily execution log or proof all property gone; p472 itself records later recovery.

author: Johnston report dated 1861-10-14
location: Harpers Ferry via Charlestown towards Winchester
content: Says army left morning June15 for Winchester and bivouacked four miles beyond Charlestown.
authority_or_effect: Reported main-column departure and first halt.
receipt_evidence: Retrospective official report.
limitation: Contemporary June15 Long Meadow letter says removal reported to Davis yesterday; retain distinct evidence, no silent single-date reconciliation.

author: Johnston report dated 1861-10-14
location: Towards Martinsburg turnpike and Bunker Hill
content: Says news of Patterson crossing and Romney withdrawal led to flank movement to Bunker Hill; same paragraph places Richmond courier authorization on June16.
authority_or_effect: Commander redirects his own march to interpose before Winchester.
receipt_evidence: Retrospective receipt claim conflicts with June15 acknowledgment.
limitation: Not permission manufactured before departure; reported enemy reaction is not independently certified here.

author: J. E. Johnston
content: Own headquarters heading names Camp Long Meadow.
authority_or_effect: Physical-location evidence for correspondence.
receipt_evidence: Own dated paper.
limitation: Read pages do not locate the camp on a precise modern coordinate or prove its identity with the four-mile bivouac.

author: J. E. Johnston; S. Cooper
content: Johnston heading names Camp Bunker Hill June17; Cooper addresses him there June18; June17 letter describes move based on June16 intelligence.
authority_or_effect: Contemporary own heading plus government address.
receipt_evidence: June17 report received June18.
limitation: Twelve-mile distance is as stated in June letter; July report p473 gives nine for later enemy position, not a new map calibration.

paper_or_event_date: after Bunker Hill; exact day unstated
author: Johnston report dated 1861-10-14
content: Says he resumed first direction/plan and proceeded to Winchester; could oppose threats from west/northeast and join Beauregard when necessary.
authority_or_effect: Own plan and reported relocation.
receipt_evidence: Retrospective official report.
limitation: No exact Winchester arrival day in this passage; do not assign June17/18/19 as proven arrival.

author: S. Cooper
content: Government addresses Johnston forces near Winchester.
authority_or_effect: Terminus-region evidence, weaker than own heading.
receipt_evidence: Outgoing address only.
limitation: Not exact receipt, presence time or original June18 letter location.

author: J. E. Johnston; Geo. Deas
content: Johnston own letter heading names Winchester; Deas letter also addresses him there.
authority_or_effect: Contemporary own headquarters heading.
receipt_evidence: No exact delivery times read.
limitation: Only heading/location used from Johnston paper; not a claim that he never temporarily moved out.

author: J. E. Johnston
content: Own headquarters heading Winchester; acknowledges June24 militia inquiry.
authority_or_effect: Independent dated location and received-paper example.
receipt_evidence: June24 letter just received by June26.
limitation: Militia criticism dispute is outside withdrawal mechanism; no strength added.

paper_or_event_date: after return to Winchester; exact day unstated
author: Johnston report dated 1861-10-14
content: Steuart Maryland battalion sent back to recover public property reportedly left; Jackson later instructed to destroy B&O rolling stock that could not be removed and bring usable stock to Winchester.
authority_or_effect: Recovery and destruction instructions separate from evacuation itself.
receipt_evidence: Retrospective official report.
limitation: No inventory, locomotive count or proof every instruction executed. Do not attribute April armory fire to June withdrawal.

author: S. Cooper
content: June13 requires Potomac bridge/platforms/trestle work and enemy-useful property destroyed, rolling stock taken, road destroyed behind retreat; June18 asks recovery of unremoved gun-stocks/barrels/tilt-hammers.
authority_or_effect: Authorized destruction/removal scope; some material still unremoved per government information.
receipt_evidence: No completion receipt read.
limitation: Instruction is not measured destruction; do not assert total armory/factory destruction or complete evacuation inventory.

author: J. E. Johnston
content: Own Winchester letter says he waited at Darkesville until yesterday, returned last night, and is preparing slight fieldworks.
authority_or_effect: Dated return after temporary forward deployment, not continuous Winchester presence.
receipt_evidence: Own dated paper.
limitation: July7 return derived from July8 yesterday [I]; no scripted date movement proposed.

author: S. Cooper; Johnston retrospective; Davis indorsement
content: July17 telegram copy addressed Winchester requests junction if practicable and leaves arrangements to discretion; Johnston says received about 1 a.m. July18 and decided to march.
authority_or_effect: Distinct later junction decision, after withdrawal and subsequent deployments.
receipt_evidence: Johnston retrospective receipt statement; telegram copy in Davis indorsement.
limitation: Not July17 receipt simply because dated July17; no shortcut to July arrival. June discretion is not July junction authority.
